question: Before 2008, a forged DNS reply had to guess a 1-in-65,536 number. How long could planting a false address in a server take?
answer: About ten seconds. Dan Kaminsky showed that an attacker could ask a server about endless made-up names, like 1.example.com and 2.example.com, each opening a fresh race to guess the number. At thousands of tries a second, a 1-in-65,536 chance comes up fast. The 2008 fix added a second random number the reply must match.
move: Long odds shrink fast when someone can take as many tries as they like.
trap: Years, because each forged reply has only a 1-in-65,536 chance.
reference: CERT Coordination Center, Vulnerability Note VU#800113: Multiple DNS implementations vulnerable to cache poisoning, 2008
